references.text: In 1 John 7:7, the reason for hatred is that Jesus testifies against the evil deeds of the world. Psalm 97:10 expresses the same principle: Those who love the Lord hate evil, which creates a natural conflict between God's people and the world.

John 7:7 explains that the world hates Jesus because he testifies against its evil deeds. In John 15:18-19 this is directly expanded: If the world hates you, know that it has hated me before it hated you. The world loves its own, but hates those who are not of the world, just as Jesus is not of the world.

In John 7:7, Jesus points out that the deeds of the world are evil. In John 8:44-47 he explains why: Your father is the devil, and he was a liar and a murderer from the beginning. They do not hear God's word because they are not of God, which confirms that their deeds are evil.

John 7:7 shows that Jesus is hated because he testifies against the evil deeds of the world. In 1 John 3:12-13 this is compared to Cain, who killed his brother because his own deeds were evil while his brother's were righteous. The world no longer hates the brothers, but the memory of the nature of this conflict remains the same.
